signal: Olo was taken private by Thoma Bravo, acquired Spendgo for loyalty, and is building the Olo Network ahead of a customer app launch.

email.body1:
Ross, saw Olo went private with Thoma Bravo, picked up Spendgo, and is standing up the Olo Network.

A take-private plus new products usually surfaces more in-market accounts than the team can act on, and signal-to-action latency is where pipeline quietly leaks. Our AI SDR turns buying signals into booked meetings with zero rep time per prospect: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new hires.

I built a signal play for Olo off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Ross, quick follow-up for Olo.

Under Thoma Bravo, efficiency pressure usually goes up, but most RevOps teams still lose days getting signals researched, written, and routed to a rep. The measurable lift comes from collapsing that latency, every email auto-logged to your CRM.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three changes I would make. Our best practices alone usually lift reply rates 50-70%.
email.body3:
Ross, last bit of proof for Olo.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, live in four weeks with every email logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Olo's reply rate likely compares to peer restaurant-tech firms. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Ross, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If turning signals into meetings faster isn't a RevOps priority right now, no problem at all. A take-private plus a network build-out is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a pipeline gap analysis scoped to Olo's motion? I will tailor it to your team either way.
